description: Run Spark code interactively via the Fabric Livy API and get structured output. `spark run` is the one-shot, agent-native primitive: it creates an interactive Livy session on the lakehouse, waits for it to become idle, runs one statement, returns the output, and ALWAYS deletes the session (even on error). Bounded by --timeout so it never hangs. Add --high-concurrency (optionally with --session-tag <tag>) to acquire a High-Concurrency session instead — concurrent runs sharing a --session-tag are packed onto ONE underlying Spark session (each with an isolated REPL). For multiple statements on one warm session, use `spark create-livy-session --wait` + `spark run-statement` + `spark delete-livy-session`. Languages: pyspark (default), scala, sql, r. This is DISTINCT from the read-only monitoring commands `spark list-livy-sessions`/`get-livy-session`.
notes: Live-verified. Output fields: 'text' is the text/plain REPL output (pyspark/scala print/repr); 'status' is 'ok' or 'error'; 'data' is the FULL output.data map; 'sessionDeleted' confirms the ephemeral session was cleaned up. With --high-concurrency the output also carries 'highConcurrency': true. IMPORTANT: Spark SQL results do NOT come back as text/plain — they arrive under data['application/json'] as {schema:{fields:[...]}, data:[[...]], truncated} (so 'text' is null for --language sql; read data['application/json']['data'] for the rows). On a Spark error the command exits non-zero and the envelope carries status='error', ename, evalue, and traceback. A cold session takes ~100s to reach 'idle' (~50s for HC), so --timeout defaults to 300s; raise it for slow starts or long jobs. HC session packing (via --session-tag) uses a SEPARATE endpoint (/highConcurrencySessions) — it is NOT a Spark --conf setting. All create/run paths consume Spark capacity while the session is alive; the one-shot `run` self-cleans, but a session created with create-livy-session MUST be deleted with delete-livy-session.
query_examples: fabio spark run --workspace <WS> --lakehouse <LH> --code "SELECT count(*) FROM sales" --language sql --query 'data."application/json".data'
